title: Digestive, Respiratory and Circulatory Systems
seo_title: Anatomy and Physiology 12: Digestive, Respiratory and Circulatory Systems Worksheets
short_title: digestion, gas exchange, the heart and blood
standard_text: Organ systems: the digestive system and enzymes, the respiratory system and gas exchange, and the heart, blood vessels and blood. (summary of BC's Curriculum, Anatomy and Physiology 12)
meta_desc: Free Anatomy and Physiology 12 worksheets (BC Curriculum): digestion, gas exchange, the heart and blood. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Digestion breaks food into molecules small enough to absorb.
key_sub: Gas exchange happens in the alveoli.
body_html:
How to think about it

Digestion breaks food down mechanically and chemically: amylase digests starch, protease digests protein and lipase digests fat. Nutrients are absorbed through the villi of the small intestine.

Air flows through the trachea, bronchi and bronchioles to the alveoli, where oxygen diffuses into the capillaries and carbon dioxide diffuses out. The heart has four chambers and pumps blood through the pulmonary and systemic circuits; arteries carry blood away from the heart and veins carry it back.

Example

Which enzyme digests starch?

Found in saliva

Answer: amylase

Example

Which chamber pumps blood to the body?

It has the thickest wall.

Answer: the left ventricle

Common mistakes

  • Thinking all arteries carry oxygenated blood (the pulmonary artery does not).
  • Thinking the stomach absorbs most nutrients.
  • Thinking veins have thick muscular walls.

faq.q: Why are alveoli so small and numerous?
faq.a: They give a huge surface area for gas exchange.

faq.q: What do valves in the heart do?
faq.a: They stop blood from flowing backward.

A person has a tidal volume of 0.40 L and breathes 10 times per minute. Calculate the pulmonary ventilation rate.
items.e: Pulmonary ventilation = tidal volume × breathing rate = 4.00 L min⁻¹.

items.q: Which part of the digestive system does this? It churns food and makes gastric juice with protease and acid to start digesting proteins.
items.e: The stomach: It churns food and makes gastric juice with protease and acid to start digesting proteins.

items.q: Where does trypsin act?
items.e: Trypsin acts in the small intestine.

items.q: Where does maltase act?
items.e: Maltase acts in the small intestine.

items.q: Food enters the small intestine. Which part did it come from?
items.e: The order is: mouth → esophagus → stomach → small intestine → large intestine → rectum → anus.

items.q: What is the role of the epithelium in the alveoli?
c: it is one cell thick, giving a short diffusion pathway
items.e: Capillary walls are also very thin.

items.q: What is the main job of the stomach?
c: It churns food and makes gastric juice with protease and acid to start digesting proteins.
It makes bile, which breaks fats into small droplets.
It makes pancreatic juice with carbohydrase, protease and lipase.
It absorbs water and mineral salts from undigested food.
items.e: The stomach: It churns food and makes gastric juice with protease and acid to start digesting proteins.

items.q: Where does pepsin act?
items.e: Pepsin acts in the stomach.

items.q: A block of agar is 1 cm × 4 cm × 10 cm. Calculate its surface area to volume ratio, as x : 1.
What is the product of digestion by pepsin?
items.e: Pepsin digests protein into polypeptides.

items.q: Where does lipase act?
items.e: Lipase acts in the small intestine.

items.q: A person has a tidal volume of 0.50 L and breathes 14 times per minute. Calculate the pulmonary ventilation rate.
items.e: Pulmonary ventilation = tidal volume × breathing rate = 7.00 L min⁻¹.

items.q: Which part of the digestive system does this? It makes bile, which breaks fats into small droplets.
items.e: The liver: It makes bile, which breaks fats into small droplets.

items.q: What is the product of digestion by lipase?
items.e: Lipase digests fats into fatty acids and glycerol.

items.q: Why do single-celled organisms not need a gas exchange system?
c: they have a large surface area to volume ratio, so diffusion is fast enough
items.e: Larger organisms need specialized surfaces.

items.q: How are monoglycerides and fatty acids absorbed into ileum cells?
c: micelles carry them to the cell, then they diffuse through the membrane
items.e: In the cell they reform triglycerides and form chylomicrons.

items.q: Pulmonary ventilation is 8.80 L min⁻¹ at 16 breaths per minute. Calculate the tidal volume.
items.e: Tidal volume = ventilation ÷ breathing rate = 0.550 L.

items.q: Food enters the stomach. Which part did it come from?
items.e: The order is: mouth → esophagus → stomach → small intestine → large intestine → rectum → anus.

items.q: What happens during normal expiration?
c: the ribs move up and out
the diaphragm and external intercostal muscles relax
items.e: Expiration is mostly passive.

items.q: Which enzyme digests proteins in the stomach?
items.e: It works best in acid conditions.

items.q: What is the effect of emphysema on gas exchange?
c: the alveoli walls break down, reducing the surface area
items.e: Elastin is damaged, so exhaling is harder.

items.q: How is air carried to the cells of an insect?
items.e: Gas exchange happens at the tracheole ends.

About what percentage of expired air is oxygen?
items.e: Inspired: 21% O₂, 0.04% CO₂. Expired: 16% O₂, 4% CO₂, saturated with water vapour.

items.q: Calculate the surface area to volume ratio of a cube with sides of 8 cm, as x : 1.
A block of agar is 3 cm × 4 cm × 5 cm. Calculate its surface area to volume ratio, as x : 1.
Why can insects not grow very large?
c: gases move along the tracheae mainly by diffusion, which is slow over long distances
items.e: Muscle movement can help ventilate the tracheae.

items.q: What do exopeptidases do?
c: remove amino acids from the ends of polypeptides
hydrolyze peptide bonds in the middle of chains
items.e: Endopeptidases act within the chain.

items.q: A person breathes 16 times a minute with a tidal volume of 450 mL. How much air does he breathe in each minute?
items.e: Pulmonary ventilation = rate × TV = 16 × 450 = 7200 mL.

items.q: A block of agar is 1 cm × 3 cm × 5 cm. Calculate its surface area to volume ratio, as x : 1.

items.e: Inspired: 21% O₂, 0.04% CO₂. Expired: 16% O₂, 4% CO₂, saturated with water vapour.

items.q: About what percentage of expired air is carbon dioxide?
items.e: Inspired: 21% O₂, 0.04% CO₂. Expired: 16% O₂, 4% CO₂, saturated with water vapour.

items.q: Why are gill filaments covered in lamellae?
c: to increase the surface area for gas exchange
items.e: Each lamella has many capillaries.

items.q: What happens during inspiration?
c: the external intercostal muscles and diaphragm contract, so the volume of the thorax increases
items.e: Air pressure in the lungs falls below atmospheric pressure.

items.q: A block of agar is 1 cm × 3 cm × 8 cm. Calculate its surface area to volume ratio, as x : 1.
How do insects reduce water loss through gas exchange?
items.e: A waxy cuticle also helps.

items.q: How does the percentage of nitrogen in expired air compare with inspired air?
items.e: Nitrogen is not used by the body.

items.q: Which blood vessel carries blood from the right ventricle to the lungs?
items.e: Arteries carry blood away from the heart; veins carry it back.

items.q: What is double circulation?
c: blood passes through the heart twice in one complete circuit: pulmonary and systemic
items.e: Found in birds and mammals.

items.q: Stroke volume is 60 mL and heart rate is 90 beats per minute. Calculate cardiac output in L min⁻¹.
items.e: Cardiac output = stroke volume × heart rate = 5400 mL min⁻¹ = 5.40 L min⁻¹.

items.q: Which part of the blood or heart is responsible for forming fibrin threads in clotting?
items.e: Fibrinogen: forming fibrin threads in clotting.

items.q: What is the role of lymphocytes?
c: B and T cells of the immune response
passing the impulse from the atria to the ventricles
items.e: Lymphocytes: B and T cells of the immune response.

items.q: Which part of the blood or heart is responsible for becoming macrophages that engulf germs?
items.e: Monocytes: becoming macrophages that engulf germs.

items.q: How many litres of blood does a healthy adult have?
items.e: Plasma is about 55% of it.

items.q: Which part of the blood or heart is responsible for releasing factors that help blood clot?
items.e: Platelets: releasing factors that help blood clot.

items.q: Does the aorta carry oxygenated or deoxygenated blood?
items.e: The aorta carries oxygenated blood from the left ventricle to the body.

items.q: Stroke volume is 120 mL and heart rate is 100 beats per minute. Calculate cardiac output in L min⁻¹.
items.e: Cardiac output = stroke volume × heart rate = 12000 mL min⁻¹ = 12.0 L min⁻¹.

items.q: What is the life span of a red blood cell?
items.e: They are destroyed in the spleen.

items.q: Cardiac output is 7.50 L min⁻¹ and heart rate is 100 beats per minute. Calculate the stroke volume in mL.
Cardiac output is 4.80 L min⁻¹ and stroke volume is 75 mL. Calculate the heart rate.
items.e: HR = CO ÷ SV = 4800 ÷ 75 = 64 beats min⁻¹.

items.q: Does the renal artery carry oxygenated or deoxygenated blood?
items.e: The renal artery carries oxygenated blood from the aorta to the kidney.

items.q: Pulmonary ventilation is 5.00 L min⁻¹ at 10 breaths per minute. Calculate the tidal volume.
items.e: Tidal volume = ventilation ÷ breathing rate = 0.500 L.

items.q: Which blood vessel carries blood from the body to the right atrium?
items.e: Arteries carry blood away from the heart; veins carry it back.

items.q: Cardiac output is 12.0 L min⁻¹ and stroke volume is 120 mL. Calculate the heart rate.
items.e: HR = CO ÷ SV = 12000 ÷ 120 = 100 beats min⁻¹.

items.q: One cardiac cycle on an ECG lasts 0.75 s. Calculate the heart rate in beats per minute.
items.e: Heart rate = 60 ÷ 0.75 = 80.0 beats min⁻¹.

items.q: Does the pulmonary vein carry oxygenated or deoxygenated blood?
items.e: The pulmonary vein carries oxygenated blood from the lungs to the left atrium.

items.q: Stroke volume is 60 mL and heart rate is 64 beats per minute. Calculate cardiac output in L min⁻¹.
items.e: Cardiac output = stroke volume × heart rate = 3840 mL min⁻¹ = 3.84 L min⁻¹.

items.q: Which substance in cigarette smoke: it joins with red blood cells and reduces how much oxygen the blood can carry.
items.e: Nicotine addicts; tar causes cancer; carbon monoxide reduces oxygen carried.

items.q: Which blood group has anti-B in its plasma?
items.e: Blood group A has anti-B in the plasma.

items.q: Which part of the blood or heart is responsible for the most abundant white blood cells (60–65%), phagocytic?
items.e: Neutrophils: the most abundant white blood cells (60–65%), phagocytic.

items.q: Stroke volume is 60 mL and heart rate is 120 beats per minute. Calculate cardiac output in L min⁻¹.
items.e: Cardiac output = stroke volume × heart rate = 7200 mL min⁻¹ = 7.20 L min⁻¹.

items.q: Which antigen is on the red blood cells of a person with blood group O?
items.e: Blood group O: no antigens on the red cells, anti-A and anti-B in the plasma.

items.q: Which blood group has anti-A and anti-B in its plasma?
items.e: Blood group O has anti-A and anti-B in the plasma.

items.q: Why does stress increase the risk of coronary heart disease?
c: Nicotine and carbon monoxide damage artery walls and raise blood pressure.
items.e: In coronary heart disease, the coronary arteries are narrowed by fatty deposits (atherosclerosis), so less oxygen reaches the heart muscle.

items.q: How many heartbeats does a healthy adult have each minute at rest?
items.e: It is set by the SA node.

items.q: What harm does particles of soot in cigarette smoke do?
c: It joins with red blood cells and reduces how much oxygen the blood can carry.
It coats the lungs and causes cancer.
They irritate the airways and damage the alveoli.
It is addictive and raises heart rate and blood pressure.

items.q: Which blood group has no antigens on its red blood cells?
items.e: Blood group O: no antigens on the red cells, anti-A and anti-B in the plasma.

items.q: Which substance in cigarette smoke: it is addictive and raises heart rate and blood pressure.
items.e: Nicotine addicts; tar causes cancer; carbon monoxide reduces oxygen carried.

items.q: What does the P-wave of an ECG show?

items.q: Which blood group has antigen A on its red blood cells?

items.q: Which blood group is the universal donor?

items.q: Which substance in cigarette smoke: it coats the lungs and causes cancer.

items.q: Why does a diet high in saturated fat and cholesterol increase the risk of coronary heart disease?
c: Nicotine and carbon monoxide damage artery walls and raise blood pressure.

items.q: Why does high blood pressure increase the risk of coronary heart disease?
c: Nicotine and carbon monoxide damage artery walls and raise blood pressure.

items.q: Which change increases the rate of transpiration?
